southern_california.text: The marine pattern is improving through the seven-day period. Typical sustained wind runs 4-13 kt; morning is favored on 4 of 7 days. Combined seas range 0.0-6.0 ft with 12-15 sec periods. Best current windows: 10-22 AM, 10-17 PM, 10-19 AM. Confidence decreases after day five; recheck the latest marine forecast before departure.

field_reports.name: Bayside Marine Monterey Bay Report
field_reports.summary: The sea bass are still being caught from 4 Mile to Davenport in 90-120 feet of water. The rock fishing was great in the deep and shallow water. The halibut has been a little slower due to the swell. The Capitola anglers are catching some sea bass as well. The bonito are on the bite in 90-100 feet of water outside the Lighthouse. There was no wind and the swell is 5 feet. The party boat from Monterey was catching rock fish when a school of blue fin came by. The party boat caught 3 out of 5 small blue fin.

field_reports.name: Fishing the North Coast
field_reports.summary: fishingthenorthcoast October 15, 2026 Chetco Estuary Shines While North Coast Rivers Wait for Rain Guide Sam Stover with a Smith River king salmon caught and released back in 2024. Small amounts of rain is in the forecast for next week, which will hopefully get the storm door pushed open. The good news is that a change in the weather pattern is on the horizon, bringing some much-needed rain. Unfortunately for anglers, the forecast still falls well short of what’s needed to open the coastal rivers to fishing. From the Smith River south to the South Fork Eel, roughly a quarter inch of rain is forecast for Monday night into Tuesday. While any rain is welcome, our parched rivers will need several inches and a series of consistent storms before they begin to open. Hopefully, this is just the beginning, and the storm door is starting to crack open. As a reminder, the low-flow hotline is no longer in service. River openings and closures can now be tracked in real time at CDFW’s North Coast Low-Flow webpage . Low-flow information for all North Coast rivers is also available here . field_reports.name: Dockside Depoe Bay Daily Report
field_reports.summary: This is a courtesy reminder that the ocean is closed to recreational boat-based crabbing October 16-November 30. Bays, beaches, estuaries, piers, tide pools, and jetties are open to crabbing year-round, barring any area closures due to elevated biotoxin in crab.

field_reports.name: Shake N' Bake Ilwaco Report
field_reports.summary: We went back to the same spot as the day before and found birds and jumpers. We stopped on birds and our sonar lit up but the fish would not bite, except for three dumb ones. What a hit or miss year. ​Mike C 10/12. Good fishing.

field_reports.name: ODFW Ocean Salmon Updates
field_reports.mode: official commercial troll catch and management updates
field_reports.summary: Tomorrow's in-season call with NMFS and the State of Oregon, to discuss Oregon's (SOF) recreational ocean salmon fisheries is cancelled. For the 2026 recreational non-mark selective coho fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, the estimated catch through September 20, 2026, is approximately 22,250 coho salmon, or 87% of the 25,700 quota. The expected coho salmon catch for Saturday September 26, 2026, which was previously adopted and remains open as scheduled, does not provide sufficient balance to add any additional days to the fishery. PREVIOUS ACTION TAKEN: • Effective Saturday, September 26, 2026, from 12:01 a.m. through September 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m., for the ocean recreational fishery from Cape Falcon to Humbug Mountain, retention of coho salmon is allowed, with a daily bag limit of two salmon (no fin clip requirement). Beginning Sunday, September 27, 2026, the season remains open through October 31, 2026, all salmon, except coho salmon, with a daily bag limit of two salmon. The minimum size for kept Chinook salmon is 24 inches in total length.
